issues.message: Exponential backtracking (proven). Severity: CRITICAL, confidence: HIGH.
issues.hint: Attack: "{%block subject%}" . "!" x n . "!endblock" Replayed on PCRE2 10.49: preg_match fails from length 32 (backtrack_limit 100000, JIT off). The risky part is: .*? Hotspot offsets: 23-26 Unbounded quantifier detected. May cause backtracking on non-matching input. Consider making it possessive (*+) or using atomic groups (?>...). Quantifier repeats a subpattern that can match empty. This creates ambiguous backtracking paths and can be catastrophic. Nested unbounded quantifiers detected. This allows exponential backtracking. Consider using atomic groups (?>...) or possessive quantifiers (*+, ++). Suggested (verify behavior): Consider using possessive quantifiers or atomic groups to limit backtracking. Suggested (verify behavior): Ensure the repeated subpattern consumes at least one character, or wrap it in (?>...) / use possessive quantifiers. Suggested (verify behavior): Replace inner quantifiers with possessive variants or wrap them in (?>...). Suggested (verify behavior): replace nested quantifiers like (a+)+ with atomic groups (?>a+) or possessive quantifiers a++. Suggested (verify behavior): use possessive quantifiers .*+ instead of .* to prevent backtracking. Test with adversarial inputs like repeated strings followed by a non-matching character.
